d: Underground place, where I guarded the prisoners. It is to end the night. Scattered through the scene, and in various mixed attitudes the Fried Prisoners, who deplore their misfortune. The little Astianatte, in whose custody some Guards watch, lies in the lap of rest. Then Andromaca escorted by Phoenicius, and followed by Attalus, and Cefisa.

Outside the palace, adjacent to delightful gardens. It is to rise the day. Cleon is at the head of the Spartan Donzelle, which armed with arches, and arrows invite to a hunt Ermione: in the end Pyrrhus, finally Great Epirenses.
Majestic palace: rich, and magnificent throne on one side. Oreste advances out of itself. Pilade causes him to calm down.

Pirro is preceded by Grandi, Guardi, and numerous court: Ermione, Phoenician, and Attalus follow him. He goes on the throne, and sits at his nod over rich Hermione stools, and Phoenician: Oreste, and Pilade in front of the throne: indi Andromaca.
Outside the palace, as before. Ermione, Cleone, in Oreste.
Choir of Grandi, and Donzelle, Pirro with Suguito, indi Andromaca, Pilade, Phoenicio, Attalo, Cefisa, and Cleon listening.

Atrium of the palace: the sea is seen from afar, and by means of an intercom on which is built magnificent loggia. Attalus, who hasty encounters Pirrus, Cleon, who comes, and listens, at Andromaca, and Cefisa.
Andromaca, then Ermione followed by Cleone, and Phoenicius.
Choir of Donzelle and Friends of Ermione, then Oreste.
Hermione in extreme agitation, then Oreste.
Pilades with his followers and sayings.
